nodes.label: The Lab: Pretend Smart Homes
nodes.rationale: Each harness runs on the Mac, is found by the app's real discovery, speaks the real protocol and prints every command, so the app can be built and tested without owning hardware.

nodes.label: Lab Home Assistant
nodes.rationale: A real Home Assistant installed into tools/lab/.ha on first run (about 1 GB) with demo devices covering every colour mode, three climate devices, fans and a thermometer; it prints its address and an access token.

nodes.label: Lab Hue Bridge Emulator
nodes.rationale: Five lamps of different kinds in three rooms plus a motion sensor with a thermometer; Enter emulates the link button, or --auto pairs without interaction for tests.

nodes.label: Lab HomeKit Bridge
nodes.rationale: Built on HAP-NodeJS with lamps, a plug, two air conditioners and a thermometer, added to the Home app with setup code 031-45-154.

nodes.label: Bluetooth Integration Stub
nodes.rationale: Run as a plain process on macOS, Home Assistant cannot use Bluetooth because macOS would stop it, so the lab replaces that integration with a stub in homeassistant/custom_components/bluetooth.

nodes.label: dns-sd Bonjour Announcement
nodes.rationale: The lab Home Assistant's own Bonjour announcements do not reach the network, so homeassistant.sh announces it with dns-sd in the same format; enough for House Control but not for a HomeKit Bridge.

nodes.label: ServiceTests Against the Lab
nodes.rationale: Unit tests cover translation to and from each platform and the hub's routing; ServiceTests additionally run against a live lab HA and Hue emulator via HOUSE_TEST_* variables.
